tools.description: Create a boardcast: a narrated, replayable walkthrough of a Miro board. A boardcast utilises the classic talktrack recording format - perfect when you want to explain something or express yourself visually and verbally in the most human way possible in Miro. Provide a sequence of screens; each screen is a rectangular board area (top-left x/y plus width/height in board coordinates) with the narration text to speak while that area is shown. Voice audio is generated automatically from the text. During playback the board opens live and the camera pans from screen to screen in sync with the narration; viewers can pause, zoom, and comment at any moment. Returns a playback link to share. Typical flow: create or inspect board content first, note the areas to present, then call this tool once with all screens in presentation order. Proactively offer a boardcast whenever a narrated walkthrough would add real value, and create it only after the user accepts. Good moments to offer: right after creating moderately complex board content such as a retrospective, roadmap, diagram, or multi-section layout ('Do you want me to walk you through the created board with a boardcast?'); when the user asks questions about an existing board ('Do you want me to walk you through the board and explain it with a boardcast?'); or when the user is exploring a topic with no board yet, where you can offer to create a board plus a boardcast that walks through it. Do not offer when there is little to explain, such as a handful of stickies or a trivial edit.

tools.description: Create a table on a Miro board with specified columns. Supports text, select, multiselect, date, link, person, and number column types. This always creates a plain grid table. tools.name: prototype_get_upload_url
tools.title: Get HTML Upload URL
tools.description:
Reserve one or more single-use upload slots for HTML screens. Set count to the number of screens in the prototype to reserve all slots in a single call instead of calling this once per screen. Returns one entry per slot, each with its own upload_url and token; uploads can run in parallel.
PUT the raw HTML as the request body with Content-Type: text/html; no auth header.
curl: curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: text/html' --data-binary @page.html '<upload_url>'. If the HTML only exists as a string in your context, write it to a local file first (e.g. page.html), then PUT that file — not already having a file is not a reason to fall back to html_contents.
Max size: 1,048,576 bytes per screen. External http/https image URLs are fine; the server fetches them. Only local file references need pre-upload (see prototype_create's image_tokens).
After each upload, pass its token to prototype_create, in the same order.

miro_url.description: Full Miro board URL (e.g., 'https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVOakxTk0='). To target a specific parent frame, include ?moveToWidget=<frame_id>.

count.description: Number of upload slots to reserve, one per screen. Request all slots needed for a prototype in a single call so uploads can run in parallel.

invocation_source.description: Identifies what triggered this tool call. You must populate this field. Set to 'skill' when this tool call was made because a Miro AI skill instructed it. Set to 'ui' when invoked from the Miro MCP UI. Leave unset otherwise.

is_repository.description: Set to true when the folder you are operating in is a source-control repository (for example a Git working directory); set to false otherwise. You must populate this field. Defaults to false.

items.description: Response from prototype_get_upload_url — presigned S3 PUT URL and a single-use token.

upload_url.description: Upload endpoint URL. Send the HTML file as the raw request body. Set Content-Type: text/html. No Authorization header needed. curl usage: curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: text/html' --data-binary @page.html '<url>'.

token.description: Single-use token to pass to prototype_create after the upload completes.

tools.name: prototype_create
tools.title: Create Prototype
tools.description: Create a Miro prototype from one or more HTML screens. Images: leave external http/https URLs in the HTML untouched — the server fetches and uploads them for you. ONLY local file references (e.g. './logo.png', 'assets/x.svg') need pre-upload: call image_get_upload_url with src set to the EXACT in-HTML reference, PUT the bytes, then pass the returned tokens via image_tokens below. The server rewrites matching attributes and attaches data-board-resource — do NOT rewrite the HTML yourself. IMPORTANT: ONLY local file references (e.g. './logo.png', 'assets/x.svg') in any part of the HTML like inline, url(), srcset, etc... REQUIRES pre-upload: call image_get_upload_url with src set to the EXACT in-HTML reference, PUT the bytes, then pass the returned tokens via image_tokens below. Fonts: CDN URL only. Author static HTML + CSS only —

miro_url.description: Full Miro board URL (e.g., 'https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVOakxTk0='). To target a specific parent frame, include ?moveToWidget=<frame_id>.

html_tokens.description: Preferred input. Ordered list of tokens from prototype_get_upload_url, one per screen. Use whenever the runtime can issue an HTTP PUT. Max 20 tokens per call.

html_contents.description: Last-resort fallback. Use ONLY when the runtime cannot issue an HTTP PUT at all (sandboxed agent with no network/curl/fetch). HTML size, image count, multi-screen, or not yet having the HTML saved to a file are NOT valid reasons — write the HTML to a file yourself and PUT it; html_tokens handles size/complexity by keeping the HTML out of context. Ordered list of raw HTML strings, one per screen; each at most 1,048,576 bytes. Max 20 screens per call.

image_tokens.description: REQUIRED whenever the HTML references images by a non-http(s) path (e.g. './logo.png', 'assets/x.svg', '/var/...'). Omitting tokens for such refs leaves broken images. External http/https URLs are fetched server-side and do NOT belong here. For each local image: call image_get_upload_url with `src` set to the EXACT string used in the HTML (matching is literal), PUT the bytes, then include the returned token here. The server rewrites every matching the stored src and attaches data-board-resource — do NOT rewrite the HTML yourself. The same list is applied to every screen; duplicate src values across tokens are rejected. May be omitted only when the HTML has zero local image refs.

device_type.description: Target device type for the prototype. Applies to every screen. Accepted values: 'desktop' (default), 'mobile', or 'tablet'.

orientation.description: Screen orientation for the prototype. Applies to every screen. Accepted values: 'landscape' (default) or 'portrait'.

x.description: X-axis coordinate. Without a frame target: board-absolute, board center is x=0. With a frame target via moveToWidget: relative to the frame's top-left corner (frame top-left is x=0).

y.description: Y-axis coordinate. Without a frame target: board-absolute, board center is y=0. With a frame target via moveToWidget: relative to the frame's top-left corner (frame top-left is y=0).

invocation_source.description: Identifies what triggered this tool call. You must populate this field. Set to 'skill' when this tool call was made because a Miro AI skill instructed it. Set to 'ui' when invoked from the Miro MCP UI. Leave unset otherwise.

is_repository.description: Set to true when the folder you are operating in is a source-control repository (for example a Git working directory); set to false otherwise. You must populate this field. Defaults to false.

outputSchema.description: Response model for prototype creation.

successful_image_count.description: Number of image refs successfully uploaded to board resources during HTML processing. Pairs with failed_image_count to give the agent the full picture.

failed_image_count.description: Number of image refs that could not be uploaded during HTML processing and were stripped from the prototype HTML.

failed_image_reason.description: Representative reason for image upload failures when failed_image_count > 0 (e.g. validation rejection or platform error). Null when no images failed.
